headline_marked: bdnews24.com editor-in-chief [[Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59]]
headline: bdnews24.com editor-in-chief Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59
summary: The veteran journalist passed away at a hospital in London after suffering a brain haemorrhage.
details: Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the editor-in-chief of the online news portal bdnews24.com, has died at a hospital in London today. He was 59 years old.
He was on a personal visit to London to meet his son when he suddenly fell ill on Thursday night.
According to reports, he suffered a brain haemorrhage and was rushed to St Bartholomew’s Hospital for emergency treatment.
He was pronounced dead at 2:23pm local time, as cited by family members and reported by bdnews24.com.
Colleagues noted that his condition had deteriorated rapidly after he suffered a stroke while in the UK.
His family has not yet decided when his body will be brought back to Bangladesh.
Details regarding his namaz-e-janaza and burial will be announced by the family at a later date.
caption:
bdnews24.com editor-in-chief Toufique Imrose Khalidi has passed away at 59 in London.

Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the editor-in-chief of the online news portal bdnews24.com, has died at a hospital in London today. He was 59 years old.

He was on a personal visit to London to meet his son when he suddenly fell ill on Thursday night.

According to reports, he suffered a brain haemorrhage and was rushed to St Bartholomew’s Hospital for emergency treatment.

He was pronounced dead at 2:23pm local time, as cited by family members and reported by bdnews24.com.

Colleagues noted that his condition had deteriorated rapidly after he suffered a stroke while in the UK.

His family has not yet decided when his body will be brought back to Bangladesh.

Details regarding his namaz-e-janaza and burial will be announced by the family at a later date.

headline_marked: Jamaat demands [[Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman's unconditional release]] after airport arrest
headline: Jamaat demands Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman's unconditional release after airport arrest
summary: The party alleges the case was filed before any investigation into a reported altercation at Dhaka airport, calling the arrest 'intentional'.
details: Former MP and retired Major Akhtaruzzaman was arrested by police following allegations of creating disorder, obstructing government duties, and assaulting a security official at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has condemned the arrest, with Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar stating that the case was filed with 'ulterior motives' before any investigation into the incident took place.
According to Jamaat, Akhtaruzzaman, a freedom fighter, was returning from Umrah when he protested against harassment and inconvenience faced by passengers at the airport.
Jamaat further claimed that two Biman Bangladesh Airlines officials had already been suspended over allegations of passenger harassment and luggage misconduct at the airport.
The party is calling for an impartial investigation into the 'ordeal' faced by passengers and demands that those responsible for mismanagement at the airport be held accountable.
Police have stated they will investigate the incident using CCTV footage, eyewitness accounts, and other evidence to determine the facts of the case.
caption:
A former MP and freedom fighter arrested over an airport altercation. Jamaat calls it a 'planned' arrest.

Former MP and retired Major Akhtaruzzaman was arrested by police following allegations of creating disorder, obstructing government duties, and assaulting a security official at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has condemned the arrest, with Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar stating that the case was filed with 'ulterior motives' before any investigation into the incident took place.

According to Jamaat, Akhtaruzzaman, a freedom fighter, was returning from Umrah when he protested against harassment and inconvenience faced by passengers at the airport.

Jamaat further claimed that two Biman Bangladesh Airlines officials had already been suspended over allegations of passenger harassment and luggage misconduct at the airport.

The party is calling for an impartial investigation into the 'ordeal' faced by passengers and demands that those responsible for mismanagement at the airport be held accountable.

Police have stated they will investigate the incident using CCTV footage, eyewitness accounts, and other evidence to determine the facts of the case.
